documentation.claim: backend-shared states that concrete Application classes of another module are forbidden across a module boundary and need an explicit allowlist entry; no legacy checker applied this to imports coming from the host app or from core-backend.
documentation.quote: **Forbidden:** importing concrete Application classes from a sibling module (actions, services, policies, exceptions). If you need cross-module access to a concrete class, first ask whether a contract interface would be more appropriate. If unavoidable, add it to `cross_module_concrete_application_allowlist` in `config/architecture.php` — but treat the allowlist as a last resort.

documentation.claim: backend-shared/src/AGENTS.md enumerates the public surface (Application\Contracts, Application\Events, Domain, Presentation) as the only cross-module entry.
the host app's own module contract requires cross-module communication through contracts/interfaces/facades, without restricting the statement to the App\Modules namespace.
documentation.quote: - Między modułami używaj kontraktów, interfejsów albo fasad modułowych.

legacy_blindness.claim: the cross-module Application check is anchored to `App\Modules\`, so an import of a concrete `LitRev\BackendShared\...\Application\` service never matches.
the Http boundary check is anchored to `App\Modules\` as well.

classification.rationale: the constraint behind `host-cross-module-public-surface` is stated in 3 documentation location(s) verified in this run; the legacy checkers that would have had to enforce it are anchored to a namespace that cannot match the offending import, so the rule existed only in prose.
classification.rule: classify_c2: prose rule exists, no legacy checker enforced it
